title: Large Language Models with Temporal Reasoning for Longitudinal Clinical Summarization and Prediction
abstract: The study evaluates open-source LLMs, retrieval-augmented variants, and chain-of-thought prompting on long patient trajectories containing structured and unstructured data spread across time. It specifically tests temporal coherence in longitudinal summarization and prediction and finds continuing difficulty with temporal progression.

admission.reason: The abstract concerns temporal reasoning over long clinical trajectories, but it does not show an incremental briefing mechanism that distinguishes changed, persistent-open, resolved, or superseded state. Its contribution overlaps the longitudinal clinical-summarization evidence already admitted without closing a distinct Topic 09 gap.

title: Reducing Physicians' Cognitive Load During Chart Review: A Problem-Oriented Summary of the Patient Electronic Record
abstract: ProSPER organizes longitudinal electronic health-record information around an automatically generated problem list and disease-specific views. Developed from 1,500 longitudinal patient records, it combines multiple NLP components to provide comprehensive problem-oriented summaries intended to reduce review burden.

admission.reason: The abstract describes another problem-oriented longitudinal EHR summarizer, but the relevant capability is substantially covered by the admitted HARVEST and CLIN-SUMM papers. It does not show a distinct incremental-state, omission/repetition, or new-versus-still-open evaluation needed to justify another reading slot.

title: Mining Sequential Update Summarization with Hierarchical Text Analysis
abstract: The paper formalizes sequential update summarization and develops a hierarchical topic- and sentence-level update-mining system. Evaluation on TREC 2013 uses expected gain, expected latency gain, comprehensiveness, and latency comprehensiveness, exposing precision/recall and timeliness tradeoffs for repeated updates.

admission.reason: The paper implements sequential update summarization on the TREC 2013 task, but its principal capability and evaluation dimensions are already represented more directly by the admitted TREC 2013 overview. The abstract does not add unresolved-state carry-forward or a distinct omission/repetition criterion that warrants an additional reading slot.

title: HLTCOE at TREC 2013: Temporal Summarization
abstract: The system addresses sequential update summarization by processing a temporally ordered stream and selecting sentences containing relevant, new, and important information. Unlike earlier batch update-summarization settings, the TREC task requires continuous and immediate updates.

admission.reason: The system selects relevant, new, and important sentences from a temporal stream, but this is an implementation of the same TREC 2013 sequential-update setting already admitted through the track overview. The abstract does not add persistent unresolved-state handling or a distinct evaluation capability.

title: On the collective classification of email "speech acts"
abstract: The paper classifies email messages for acts such as requests and commitments while exploiting sequential correlations among messages in the same thread. A dependency-network collective classifier improves classification for some email-act categories over a bag-of-words baseline.

admission.reason: The paper detects email speech acts such as requests and commitments, but Topic 09 does not own extraction of requests or commitments. The abstract does not study briefing selection, prioritization, reminder value, longitudinal carry-forward, or user-facing task management, so the vocabulary overlap is insufficient.

title: Generalizing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution Across Multiple Corpora
abstract: The paper evaluates cross-document event-coreference systems across several corpora rather than within a single dataset. It finds substantial domain-dependent behavior and overfitting, and argues that broadly applicable multi-document identity resolution requires multi-corpus evaluation.

admission.reason: VERIFIED identity, but the contribution is cross-document event-coreference robustness rather than briefing selection or longitudinal prioritization. Stable cross-thread identity is an upstream Topic 03 responsibility in the project context; admitting this paper here would duplicate that ownership rather than strengthen a Topic 09 stream.

title: A Multi-level System for Sequential Update Summarization
abstract: The paper develops a multi-level system that combines topic-level and sentence-level analysis to produce useful, new, and timely updates about developing events. It evaluates the approach using the TREC Temporal Summarization sequential-update task.

admission.reason: The abstract describes another topic- and sentence-level implementation of the TREC Temporal Summarization task. Its core capability is redundant with the admitted TREC overview and does not add treatment of persistent unresolved state, personalization, or a new evaluation dimension.

title: Constructive Preference Elicitation
abstract: The paper studies interactive learning of user preferences in decision spaces where feasible outcomes are delimited by explicit hard requirements. Preference learning operates over the feasible space while constrained optimization preserves non-negotiable requirements, offering a mechanism for separating hard user rules from softer learned preferences.

admission.reason: The paper separates explicit hard requirements from learned preferences and is relevant in principle, but that transfer capability is already represented more directly by the admitted soft-versus-hard-bounds preference-learning candidate. The abstract does not add evidence specific to briefing, email obligations, or comparative outcomes from separating the two signal classes.

title: Learning to Classify Email into “Speech Acts”
abstract: The paper learns to classify email by sender intent using categories such as propose, commit, deliver, meeting, information, and task. The motivating applications include tracking ongoing joint activities, commitments, requests, deadlines, delegated subtasks, and reminders from ordinary unstructured email.

admission.reason: The motivating applications mention commitments, tasks, deadlines, and reminders, but the actual contribution is classification of email speech acts. That belongs to upstream extraction of work semantics rather than Topic 09's longitudinal selection, prioritization, reminder scheduling, or briefing evaluation.
